documents.title: Proposed AI Guidelines
documents.summary: University-wide draft guidelines for all community members covering data confidentiality, bias, disclosure, accountability, equity, IP, safety, notetaking tools, classroom, workplace and research use. It sets no classroom rule itself and leaves prohibit, allow-with-attribution or encourage to faculty. It says it is not a final policy.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines say "Villanova University does not restrict the use of AI tools in the classroom. Faculty and instructors may choose to prohibit, to allow with attribution, or to encourage generative AI use." The document sets no stance of its own and hands the choice to instructors, so it delegates.

units.why: The purpose section says Villanova "has an obligation to equip students and graduates" with tools for a world of emerging technologies; this is a career-readiness rationale, so P44, informs, general.
units.anchor: Villanova has an obligation to equip students and graduates, as well as employees and researchers
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded actor admin and unit_stance neutral; coder B coded actor all and unit_stance encourage. The Purpose section is the university stating its own obligation ("Villanova has an obligation to equip students and graduates"), so the actor is admin; it is a rationale and takes no position on AI use, so unit_stance is neutral (informs), not encourage. Type P44 is agreed.

units.why: The guidelines "aim to foster an ethical and responsible approach to AI" balancing innovation with named principles; a statement of purpose and principles is P56.
units.anchor: foster an ethical and responsible approach to AI, balancing innovation with the core principles
units.resolution_why: Coders split on actor (A admin, B all). The sentence says what "These Guidelines aim to" do, which is the issuing office stating its purpose, not a duty on community members, so admin. P56 is agreed.

units.why: The scope sentence says the guidelines apply to "all members of the Villanova University community"; it sets coverage of the framework, so P56 rather than P61 (it defines people, not AI).
units.anchor: apply to the use of AI tools by all members of the Villanova University community

units.why: The document says it "is not a final policy but will be updated as AI technology, regulations, and industry practices evolve", a provisional-policy statement, P54.

units.resolution_why: Coders split on actor (A admin, B all). "It is intended to complement existing policies" describes the guidelines document, i.e. the issuing body, so admin. P77 and informs are agreed.

units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. The source defines "AI System" as "Any system, software, hardware, application, tool, or utility that operates in whole or in part using AI", a real scope definition, so kept as P61, informs.

units.resolution_why: Types and modality agree (P77, should). Unit_stance split (A neutral, B restrict). The sentence only points AI use to the Acceptable Use and Data Classifications policies and does not itself limit any use, so neutral.

So P50, with fit_note kept for the approval and contract conditions. The anchor omits the sensitive-data subject, so coder B's normalized policy is kept.

The anchor states the rule, so policy is null.

Per the constant-comparison rule, UNCOVERED with the note is kept. "Be aware" is advice, so should.

documents.title: The Code of Academic Integrity
documents.summary: The university Code of Academic Integrity defines cheating, plagiarism and dishonesty, with AI written into several definitions, and lists penalties and appeal. Unsanctioned or undocumented AI assistance counts as dishonesty, and central assignment tasks need instructor permission and attribution, while faculty may set course rules.
documents.stance_why: The Code says cheating includes "using the assistance of A.I. text generators to perform central requirements of an assignment ... without both the explicit permission of the instructor and complete attribution and citation". AI is barred unless permitted and cited, so the stance is restrict, even though faculty may set course rules.

units.why: Academic dishonesty includes representing as one's own work "work generated through unsanctioned and/or undocumented artificial intelligence (A.I.) assistance"; AI is barred only when unsanctioned or undocumented, so P36, must-not, restrict.
units.anchor: including work generated through unsanctioned and/or undocumented artificial intelligence (A.I.) assistance
units.resolution_why: Unit_stance split (A prohibit, B restrict). Only unsanctioned or undocumented AI work is called dishonest, so sanctioned and documented AI use remains allowed: restrict, not prohibit. This matches the document stance restrict.

units.why: "students must submit work that they have completed themselves in accordance with the guidelines for the course"; work must be the student's own, P29.
units.anchor: students must submit work that they have completed themselves
units.resolution_why: Phase split (A during-work, B general). The duty to "submit work that they have completed themselves" attaches to submitting assignments, so during-work.

units.why: "faculty may set specific rules about what is and is not allowed in a particular course and on a given assignment"; per-instructor rules, P04.

units.fit_note: Does not name AI; applies to any faculty-issued instructions, which include AI rules.

units.fit_note: A general rule on unapproved help for individual assessments, not specific to a silent syllabus or to AI. / Covers outside help generally, not AI by name.
units.resolution_why: Phase split (A during-assessment, B during-work). The sentence covers any "individual class assessment (i.e. assignment, quiz, lab report, exam, etc.)", and assignments come first, so it is not limited to exams; during-work. Type P06 agreed; both fit notes kept.

units.why: Using "A.I. text generators to perform central requirements of an assignment ... without both the explicit permission of the instructor and complete attribution and citation" is cheating; AI doing the central work needs prior instructor permission, so P107, must-not, restrict.
units.anchor: without both the explicit permission of the instructor and complete attribution and citation
units.policy: Students do not use A.I. text generators to perform central requirements of an assignment (reading, synthesizing, interpreting, writing, coding, programming) without both the explicit permission of the instructor and complete attribution and citation of A.I.-assisted components.
units.fit_note: Lists central requirements (reading, synthesizing, interpreting, writing, coding, programming); permission is required plus citation. / Also lists reading and synthesizing as central requirements and requires both permission and citation.
units.resolution_why: This sentence was coded as three overlapping units: A's permission unit (P107), B's whole-sentence unit (P19) and B's permission unit (P06). One sentence states one rule on AI doing central requirements, conditional on explicit permission, so they are merged into this unit; the citation requirement stays as its own unit. P107 chosen over P19 because the sentence does not ban such use outright, it requires prior instructor permission, and over P06 because it names AI. Coder B's normalized policy is kept because the anchor omits the central-requirements part; B's fit_note kept.

units.why: The same sentence requires "complete attribution and citation of A.I.-assisted components" when AI is used; a citation duty, P24.
units.anchor: complete attribution and citation of A.I.-assisted components
units.resolution_why: Coder A (anchor "complete attribution and citation of A.I.-assisted components") coded P24, must, require; coder B coded the same passage P24, must, permit. Type and modality agree; unit_stance is permit because AI use is allowed once it is attributed, consistent with other P24 units. Coder B's separate P06 unit on the same sentence is merged into the previous unit.

units.why: "Please consult with your instructor if you are uncertain whether outside sources/support, including A.I. support, are allowed" is ask-when-unsure, P10.
units.anchor: Please consult with your instructor if you are uncertain whether outside sources/support
units.frag_end: allowed in a course or on an assignment

units.why: Plagiarism "includes work generated by or originating from non-human sources, such as A.I."; AI-generated work is classed as plagiarism, P36.
units.anchor: This includes work generated by or originating from non-human sources, such as A.I.
units.resolution_why: Modality split (A informs, B must-not). "Plagiarism ... includes work generated by or originating from non-human sources, such as A.I." is a definition of what counts as plagiarism, so informs, neutral. The prohibition itself is coded on the units that say what students must not do.

units.why: "Unacknowledged appropriation involves using either the work of another person or of A.I. without reference or acknowledgement"; AI use without acknowledgement is plagiarism, so P36, must-not, restrict (acknowledged use is not barred).
units.anchor: using either the work of another person or of A.I. without reference or acknowledgement
units.resolution_why: Coder A chose P36, when-misuse, unit_stance prohibit; coder B chose P45 (treat AI like a human collaborator), during-work, restrict. The passage defines unacknowledged use of AI as a form of plagiarism, which is what P36 collects, and it does not bar acknowledged use, so restrict not prohibit. Phase when-misuse because it defines the violation. P45 fits less well because the sentence classifies a violation instead of setting collaborator-style rules.

units.why: Unacknowledged appropriation includes "borrowing sentences, phrases, and paragraphs from outside sources, including A.I. text generators"; AI may not supply the text one submits, P19 (conditioned on acknowledgement).
units.anchor: borrowing sentences, phrases, and paragraphs from outside sources, including A.I. text generators
units.fit_note: The ban applies to unacknowledged borrowing; acknowledged use is not addressed here.

units.why: Sources requiring citation include "ideas, summaries, drafts, data, code, and text generated via A.I."; AI output must be cited, P24.
units.anchor: ideas, summaries, drafts, data, code, and text generated via A.I.
units.resolution_why: Unit_stance split (A require, B permit). The list names AI-generated ideas, code and text as sources that must be cited; AI use is allowed with citation, so permit, consistent with other P24 units.

units.why: Students "should contact the instructor to discuss this prior to submission" if uncertain whether they acknowledged sources adequately, ask-when-unsure, P10.
units.anchor: they should contact the instructor to discuss this prior to submission
units.fit_note: Concerns source acknowledgement in general; AI is named elsewhere in the section.

units.why: "it is the student’s responsibility to authenticate authorship" when authorship is questioned; students own their work, P29.
units.anchor: it is the student’s responsibility to authenticate authorship
units.fit_note: Also sets who bears the burden of proving authorship in a dispute.

units.why: "Students should save evidence of their authorial process, such as drafts, notes, version histories, and transcripts of A.I. assistance" requires keeping logs, P26.

units.why: "Typically, a student with two Class I violations will be dismissed from the University"; a stated penalty, P37.

documents.unit: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
documents.title: ECE syllabus outline template: AI Policy block
tiers: AI-generated content permitted for listed uses (first draft, outline, other)
documents.summary: A short instructor-facing template in the ECE syllabus outline tool. It offers three alternative AI statements (ban, allow, allow for listed uses) and a disclosure paragraph for when AI is allowed. It is a generic template, not a particular course's policy.
documents.stance_why: The template says "choosing one of the following statements, modifying as desired" and offers a ban, an allow, and an allow for listed uses. It sets no single stance and hands the choice to the instructor, so it delegates with three tiers.

units.why: Introductory instruction to the instructor: "you should edit this part, choosing one of the following statements"; the instructor selects and adapts the AI rule, P04.
units.anchor: you should edit this part, choosing one of the following statements, modifying as desired
units.resolution_why: Unit_stance split (A neutral, B permit). The line tells the instructor to pick among statements and takes no position on AI itself, so neutral.

units.why: "The use of AI-generated content is not permitted in this course" is a course-wide ban, P01.
units.anchor: The use of AI-generated content is not permitted in this course.
units.resolution_why: Actor split (A student, B instructor). The statement is written for the syllabus and says "AI-generated content is not permitted in this course", binding students, so student.

units.why: "Its use will result in an academic integrity violation and a zero on the assignment" states a concrete penalty, P37.
units.anchor: Its use will result in an academic integrity violation and a zero on the assignment.
units.resolution_why: Modality split (A informs, B must). "Its use will result in an academic integrity violation and a zero on the assignment" states a consequence rather than commanding anyone, so informs, neutral. Actor student agreed.

units.why: "The use of AI-generated content is allowed in this course" is a permit-by-default option, P02.
units.anchor: The use of AI-generated content is allowed in this course.
units.resolution_why: Actor split (A student, B instructor). The permission statement is for the syllabus and applies to students, so student.

units.why: "permitted as follows: (a) for generating a first draft or (b) for generating an outline or (c) for generating XXX" limits AI to a closed list of tasks chosen by the instructor, P107.
units.anchor: permitted as follows: (a) for generating a first draft or (b) for generating an outline
units.fit_note: Instructor fills in the list; first draft and outline are the example uses.
units.resolution_why: Actor split (A student, B instructor). The restriction to listed uses is for the syllabus and applies to students, so student.

units.why: "you must identify the AI tool used to assist in generating your work" even after heavy editing; disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: you must identify the AI tool used to assist in generating your work
units.resolution_why: Unit_stance split (A require, B permit). The duty applies only "if AI is allowed", so AI use is permitted conditional on identifying the tool; permit.

units.why: "provide the name of the tool, date used, and prompts used to generate the output" lists specific citation details, P25.
units.anchor: provide the name of the tool, date used, and prompts used to generate the output
units.resolution_why: Unit_stance split (A require, B permit). Same reasoning as the previous unit: applies only when AI is allowed, so permit.

units.why: "you must keep a copy of the original output and provide it when requested"; keep and submit the output, P26.
units.anchor: you must keep a copy of the original output and provide it when requested
units.resolution_why: Unit_stance split (A require, B permit). Same reasoning: applies only when AI is allowed, so permit.

units.why: "you are responsible for authenticating your authorship" if questions arise; students own their work, P29.
units.anchor: you are responsible for authenticating your authorship

units.anchor: Guidelines for Students Regarding Responsible Academic Use of AI-Generated Material

notes: Course layer deferred in collect file. Template text contains LaTeX markup; anchors quote it as is. The ECE template is generic despite the ECE-3040 URL. | Coder B: Coder B. The Guidelines are headed "Proposed" and say they are not a final policy. The ECE block is a template with LaTeX markup, not a course policy. Code stance is a judgment call: restrict because it bans unsanctioned AI on central requirements by default, while leaving course rules to faculty.
